title: Redis
subtitle: Read hot data. Analyze it with SQL.
intro: Query Redis strings, hashes and lists from DuckDB, or snapshot operational data into local tables for analysis. Every Redis call selects a named DuckDB secret, keeping connection details separate from the data-access expression.

reference.name: redis_get(key, secret)
reference.description: Read a string; redis_set writes a key and value.

reference.name: redis_hget(key, field, secret)
reference.description: Read one hash field; redis_hset writes one and returns the count of fields added.

reference.name: redis_hgetall(key, secret)
reference.description: Return a table with field and value columns.

reference.name: redis_lrange_table(key, start, stop, secret)
reference.description: Return list positions and values; stop = -1 includes the end.

reference.name: redis_scan(cursor, pattern, count, secret)
reference.description: Return next_cursor:keys_csv; repeat until the returned cursor is zero.

reference.name: redis_hscan_over_scan(pattern, fields, n, secret)
reference.description: Stream key, field and value rows from matching hashes.

reference.name: redis_exists(key, secret)
reference.description: Check existence; redis_type reports the stored value type.

reference.name: redis_expire(key, seconds, secret)
reference.description: Set a TTL; redis_expireat takes a Unix timestamp and redis_ttl reads the remaining seconds.

notes.title: Choose table-shaped results
notes.body: Use redis_hgetall and redis_lrange_table for relational results. Scalar redis_mget and redis_lrange return comma-separated strings. redis_get and redis_hget return NULL for a missing key or field (wrap them in coalesce for a default); redis_mget keeps an empty entry for each missing key so positions match the requested keys.

notes.title: Scope scans and connections
notes.body: Key listing uses cursor-based SCAN, never KEYS, but redis_keys and redis_hscan_over_scan walk every page; narrow the pattern on large keyspaces. A scan is not a transactionally consistent snapshot while Redis changes. The documented transport is single-node plain TCP; configure the connection and network boundary accordingly.
